text:
priya_acme: Hey — our mobile app is hitting SSE disconnects mid-response when the phone swaps from LTE -> Wi‑Fi. Client sees ERR_SSE_CLOSED and we get partial JSON (stream cuts off in the middle). Happens reliably on iOS 16. Any ideas?

sam_support: sorry to hear that. quick Qs: which SDK or raw EventSource? token TTL? are you using a proxy/load balancer in front of us?

priya_acme: EventSource in JS (React Native WebView). Token TTL is 60s, we refresh on 55s. No customer-side proxy but traffic goes through corporate mobile carrier NAT. Happens ~2-3s after network change. Repro steps: 1) start generation 2) flip Wi‑Fi on 3) stream closes with partial chunk.

jordan_eng: common culprits: carrier NAT or mobile stack tearing the TCP without proper FIN, or the client reconnect code racing with token refresh. can you paste your EventSource init? any keepalive headers?

priya_acme: pasted snippet:
```
const es = new EventSource(url, { withCredentials: true });
es.onmessage = (e) => { /* accumulate chunks */ };
es.onerror = (e) => { console.log('ERR', e); es.close(); }
```
we don't send heartbeats from client.

sam_support: thanks. could you also share a sample server-side response fragment (what partial JSON looks like) and the client console log? even a single example helps.

priya_acme: sample partial delivered:
```
{ "id": "resp_123", "choices": [ { "text": "The quick brown fox jumps over the la"
```
client log: `EventSource error: message: 'The connection was closed'`

jordan_eng: that looks like connection got torn before final chunk. Two suggestions to triage:
- Try reproducing with direct cellular -> Wi‑Fi flip on a lab device (no company VPN) to rule out corporate NAT.
- Enable a lightweight server heartbeat (send `:\n` or `: keepalive` SSE comments every 10s) to keep NAT state alive during the transition.
Also: check any intermediate proxy (gateway/ingress) idle timeouts (Envoy idle_timeout, Nginx proxy_read_timeout).

devon_oncall: adding: if token refresh runs at same time as reconnect you'll hit a race where client closes old ES and immediately opens new one but we reject new connection because token cache hasn't updated. try staggering refresh or use silent token refresh that does not close connection until new one established.

priya_acme: ok will try heartbeats + stagger refresh. question: will partial chunks still be billed? customer asks because partial output sometimes contains almost full text but cutoff.

sam_support: billing note: usage is measured server-side tokens generated. if generation finished server-side but client disconnected before receiving full stream, it may still be billed. if generation aborted server-side (worker killed due to socket reset) that may not be billed. we'll confirm exact invoice behavior for your account and follow up.

jordan_eng: small repro we use locally: on a linux device run:
```
sudo tc qdisc add dev wlp3s0 root netem loss 10% delay 100ms
# toggle interface: nmcli networking off; sleep 2; nmcli networking on
```
That flips routes and usually triggers the same tear. If you can reproduce, grab a tcpdump on the client (500ms ring buffer) and a server side connection log. Look for TCP RST or half-close (FIN) from client side.

priya_acme: did the heartbeat change and staggering — initial quick test looks better, fewer aborted streams. will run full repro tomorrow and attach tcpdump if it still fails. thank you. :pray:

streaming-bot: Automated note: created ticket INF-7821 and assigned to eng-runtime for deeper investigation.

devon_oncall: will take INF-7821. next steps from our side: check load-balancer timeout, enable optional server side `X-Stream-Heartbeat` header that clients can opt into, and review token refresh codepath for race.

priya_acme: great, will add tcpdump + reproducible steps to the ticket if it recurs. thanks everyone.

sam_support: marking as triaged. if you hit regression, ping this thread and we'll escalate priority. :thumbsup:
